question: if i accidentally ate while fasting because i forgot, is my fast broken?
gold_answer: No. The Prophet (peace be upon him) said that whoever eats or drinks forgetfully while fasting should complete the fast, because it is Allah who fed him and gave him drink (Abu Huraira, Bukhari 6669, Muslim 2716).
must_not: claiming the fast must be made up with expiation
notes: Single clear hadith, in Bukhari and Muslim; tirmidhi 721 is parallel. Intentional eating is a different case.

question: Does a woman have to make up the prayers she missed during her period, or only the fasts?
gold_answer: Aisha reported that in the Prophet's time women were told to make up missed fasts but were not told to make up missed prayers. She rebuked the questioner who asked, saying 'Are you a Haruri?' (Nasai 2318, Tirmidhi 787).
must_not: saying missed prayers must be made up
notes: Haruri = Khawarij-like sect that insisted on it. Clear in Aisha's report.

question: what is the kaffara if someone has sex with his wife in the day in ramadan
gold_answer: In the hadith of the man who said he had intercourse with his wife in Ramadan, the Prophet asked him in order to free a slave, else fast two consecutive months, else feed sixty poor people. When he could do none, dates were brought and he was told to feed his family with them (Bukhari 1937, Muslim 2599).
must_not: a single fixed fine regardless of ability
notes: Order of the three options and the dates episode are in Bukhari 1937; Muslim 2599 lists the options.

question: Do I have to recite Al-Fatiha when I pray behind an imam? I heard scholars disagree.
gold_answer: There are two lines of evidence. Those who require it cite Ubadah's hadith: the Prophet told the congregation not to recite behind the imam except Umm al-Kitab (Abu Dawud 823). Those who say the imam's recitation suffices cite 'Whoever has an imam, the recitation of the imam is his recitation' (Ibn Majah 850) and the verse 'when the Quran is recited, give ear to it and pay heed' (7:204). The corpus presents both lines; the weighing between them is for scholars.
must_not: presenting only one view as the sole position
notes: Real fiqh disagreement; school-by-school attribution is not in the corpus, so the answer presents evidences only.

question: Can I combine Dhuhr with Asr at home when there's no travel or rain but it's hard for me?
gold_answer: Ibn Abbas reported that the Prophet combined Dhuhr with Asr and Maghrib with Isha in Medina without fear or rain, and when asked why said it was so his community would not be in hardship (Tirmidhi 187, Nasai 602). Another report of a combination in Medina has a narrator guessing that it may have been rainy nights (Bukhari 543). Scholars differ on whether this permits combining for need or hardship; consult a scholar for your case.
must_not: saying joining is freely allowed with no reason
notes: Disputed: permission for hardship vs only for rain/travel. Evidences from corpus only.

question: is wiping over socks allowed in wudu?
gold_answer: Yes. Reports say the Messenger of Allah performed ablution and wiped over his leather socks (Hudhaifah, Ibn Majah 544), and Umar told Sa'd's nephew that they used to wipe over leather socks with the Messenger of Allah (Ibn Majah 546).
must_not: claiming the Prophet never did this
notes: Details of duration and conditions are not asserted here.

question: Quran says wash the feet in wudu but I heard some people only wipe them. What do the hadith say?
gold_answer: In this translation 5:6 says to wash the feet up to the ankles. The Prophet saw a man who did not wash his heel and said 'Woe to the heels because of Hell-fire' (Muslim 573; Ibn Majah 453). The corpus also has reports of wiping over leather socks, which is a separate allowance. Differences exist between groups over wiping versus washing; present the texts and ask a scholar.
must_not: saying the Prophet wiped bare feet without any source
notes: Neutral on Sunni/Shia difference: corpus gives text of 5:6 (Pickthall: wash) and the heel hadith; no Shia source in corpus.

question: I'm sick and can't stand for fard salah. How should I pray?
gold_answer: Imran ibn Husain, who had a fistula, was told by the Prophet to pray standing; if unable then sitting; and if unable then on his side (Abu Dawud 952).
must_not: saying the prayer is dropped
notes: Order standing, sitting, side is in the hadith.

question: Do I have to fast Ramadan while travelling? My friends say you must, others say you can skip.
gold_answer: The Quran says whoever is sick or on a journey fasts the same number of other days, and that Allah desires ease, not hardship (2:185). Anas reported that on journeys with the Prophet in Ramadan, neither the fasting nor the non-fasting person criticised the other (Muslim 2620).
must_not: calling the one who breaks fast a sinner
notes: Whether fasting or breaking is better is debated; the gold only states what the texts say.

question: can a husband kiss his wife while fasting
gold_answer: Aisha reported that the Prophet used to kiss and embrace his wives while fasting, and that he had the greatest control over his desire among them (Bukhari 1927, Muslim 2576). Jabir in Bukhari adds a comment about discharge after looking at one's wife.
must_not: saying the fast is automatically invalid
notes: Scholars discuss it relative to a person's self-control; the gold does not go beyond the reports.

question: What is the virtue of fasting on the day of Arafah?
gold_answer: Abu Qatada reported the Prophet saying he hoped Allah would expiate with it the sins of the previous year and the following year (Ibn Majah 1730, Tirmidhi 749).
must_not: saying pilgrims at Arafah should fast it
notes: Wording is hope for forgiveness, 'I anticipate/hope'. Not about those at Arafah.

question: Can women go to the mosque, or can their husbands forbid them?
gold_answer: The Prophet said not to prevent your women from the mosques, though their houses are better for them (Abu Dawud 567); when women ask permission to go, do not prevent them (Muslim 988). Aisha also said that had he seen what women later innovated he would have prevented them, as Israelite women were (Abu Dawud 569).
must_not: saying women are forbidden from mosques
notes: Aisha's remark is a Companion's opinion, not a Prophetic command.

question: how serious is it to skip jummah prayer without a reason
gold_answer: Reports in Ibn Majah say that whoever abandons Friday prayer three times, for no necessary reason or through neglect, Allah seals his heart (Ibn Majah 1126, 1125).
must_not: saying the person becomes a disbeliever
notes: Hadith text only; grading not asserted here.

question: Is Witr wajib or sunnah? What is the evidence either way?
gold_answer: Ali said Witr is not definite like the prescribed prayers but the Prophet prayed it and said 'O people of the Quran, pray Witr, for Allah is Witr and loves the odd' (Ibn Majah 1169). The Prophet also taught that night prayer is in pairs and one rak'ah makes it odd if dawn is near (Muslim 1750). Scholars differ whether the command makes it obligatory or confirmed sunnah; Ali's statement is cited by those who say it is not obligatory.
must_not: asserting a single universally agreed ruling
notes: Disputed. Ali's statement is a Companion statement.

question: How long can a traveller keep shortening salah? Is there a set number of days?
gold_answer: Ibn Abbas said that the Prophet stayed 19 days on a journey shortening prayer, and that they shorten if they stay up to 19 days but pray full if longer (Bukhari 4299). Ibn Abbas also said prayer was enjoined as four rak'ahs at home and two when travelling (Nasai 1532). Scholars differ on the limit and on distance; no single figure is asserted here.
must_not: stating one limit as agreed by all
notes: Reported Ibn Abbas practice; the limit is disputed.

question: what is the minimum amount for zakat on silver or camels/dates?
gold_answer: Abu Sa'id al-Khudri reported the Prophet said no zakat is due on less than five uqiyas (awaq) of silver, less than five camels, and less than five wasqs of produce (Bukhari 1405, Muslim 2266). A wasq is 60 sa' (Bukhari 1405 note).
must_not: claiming zakat is due on any amount
notes: Nisab for silver as five awaq; conversion to modern units not asserted.

question: who can receive zakat according to the quran?
gold_answer: Surah 9:60 lists the recipients: the poor and the needy, those who collect it, those whose hearts are to be reconciled, captives, debtors, in the cause of Allah, and the wayfarer; it is a duty from Allah.
must_not: adding a ninth category
notes: Eight categories. How some categories apply today is for scholars.

question: what happens to someone who has wealth but doesn't pay its zakat?
gold_answer: The Prophet said the stored wealth whose zakat is unpaid will appear on the Day of Resurrection as a bald poisonous snake pursuing its owner (Bukhari 6957). Ibn Umar explained that verses on hoarding gold and silver came before the zakat verses, and that zakat made wealth purified (Bukhari 1404).
must_not: saying all savings are forbidden regardless of zakat
notes: Bukhari 1404 supplies Ibn Umar's explanation that paid zakat removes the kanz threat.

question: is taking and giving interest haram? what did the prophet say
gold_answer: Ibn Mas'ud reported that the Messenger of Allah cursed the one who consumes riba, the one who gives it, the witnesses and the recorder (Tirmidhi 1206; also Nasai 5105).
must_not: saying only the lender is blamed
notes: Clear and well-attested; what counts as riba in modern products is a separate scholarly matter.

question: What does Surah Al-Baqarah say about riba and the warning to those who continue it?
gold_answer: 2:275 says Allah permits trade and forbids usury, and those who return to it are rightful owners of the Fire. 2:279 says that if they do not give it up they are warned of war from Allah and His Messenger, but if they repent they keep their principal without interest, neither wronging nor being wronged.
must_not: saying only compound interest is forbidden
notes: Pickthall translation. Wording of 'war from Allah and His Messenger' is in 2:279.

question: Can I swap 10g of old gold for 10g of new gold plus some cash for the better quality?
gold_answer: The Prophet said not to sell gold for gold unless equal in weight, but gold for silver as you like (Bukhari 2175). Umar's report adds that gold for gold is riba unless handed over on the spot (Abu Dawud 3348). So a surplus in an exchange of the same commodity is the problem the hadith address; apply to your case with a scholar.
must_not: saying unequal swaps of same type are fine
notes: The question's case is a classic riba al-fadl scenario; gold only states the rule from the hadith.

question: what's gharar in business deals, why is it banned?
gold_answer: Reports say the Prophet forbade gharar sales (uncertain, risky transactions) and the pebble sale (hasah) (Tirmidhi 1230; Ibn Majah 2195 on gharar). Abu Dawud 3376 likewise reports the prohibition of a sale involving risk or uncertainty and a transaction decided by throwing stones.
must_not: claiming all risk is forbidden
notes: Hadith text alone; scope of gharar (what level is tolerated) belongs to fiqh.

question: Is all alcohol haram or just wine?
gold_answer: Ibn Umar reported the Prophet said every intoxicant is khamr and every intoxicant is forbidden (Muslim 5218, Ibn Majah 3390).
must_not: permitting small amounts of non-grape drinks
notes: Clear text; quantity rulings are not asserted.

question: does the quran ban gambling?
gold_answer: Surah 5:90 says strong drink and games of chance, idols and divining arrows are an infamy of Satan's handiwork and tells believers to leave it aside. Abu Dawud 3685 adds the Prophet forbade khamr, maysir (game of chance) and others.
must_not: saying it is only discouraged
notes: Exact application to modern lotteries/stocks is for scholars.

question: Can Muslims eat meat slaughtered by Christians and Jews?
gold_answer: Surah 5:5 says the food of those given the Scripture is lawful for Muslims and their food is lawful for them. Ibn Abbas said that the rule of not eating from what Allah's name was not pronounced on was lessened by this verse (Abu Dawud 2817). Details of how it is applied to modern slaughter are disputed and need a scholar.
must_mention: food of the People of the Book
must_not: saying all non-Muslim meat is haram or all is halal without conditions
notes: Application to industrial slaughter is not covered by the texts.

question: are lions, hawks and other predators haram to eat?
gold_answer: Ibn Abbas reported the Prophet forbade every fanged beast of prey and every bird with talons (Muslim 4994, Abu Dawud 3803).
must_not: permitting wild cats as halal
notes: Text states the general rule.

question: Is dhab (the spiny-tailed lizard) halal? I see conflicting hadith.
gold_answer: The corpus has two types of reports: Abdur-Rahman ibn Shibl said the Prophet forbade eating lizard flesh (Abu Dawud 3796), while Ibn Umar reports that when asked he said 'I neither eat it, nor do I prohibit it' (Muslim 5028). Scholars weigh these differently, which is the source of the disagreement.
must_not: claiming consensus
notes: Disputed. Gold gives the two reports only.

question: a dog licked my cup, what do i do?
gold_answer: Abu Huraira reported the Prophet said to wash the vessel seven times when a dog licks it (Ibn Majah 364). Abdullah ibn Mughaffal's report adds rubbing with dust the eighth time (Ibn Majah 365).
must_not: saying a single rinse is enough
notes: Variant reports about which wash has dust: Nasai 339 says the first.

question: What does the Quran allow of forbidden food in an emergency?
gold_answer: Surahs 2:173 and 6:145 list carrion, blood and swine flesh and what is dedicated to other than Allah, and then say whoever is compelled, neither craving nor transgressing, bears no sin and Allah is Forgiving, Merciful.
must_not: saying anything is allowed whenever one wishes
notes: Quranic necessity rule.

question: is rabbit meat permitted? someone told me its haram
gold_answer: Muhammad ibn Safwan caught two rabbits, slaughtered them with a Marwah as he had no knife, and the Prophet told him to eat them (Nasai 4399, Ibn Majah 3244).
must_not: calling rabbits haram
notes: Reported permission; narrations are cited without grading claims.

question: Why do Muslims eat with the right hand?
gold_answer: The Prophet said to eat with the right hand and drink with the right hand because Satan eats and drinks with his left (Muslim 5265, Tirmidhi 1800).
notes: Manners of eating.

question: can i drink from a gold or silver cup
gold_answer: Hudhaifa reported the Prophet forbade drinking from gold and silver vessels and eating from them, and wearing silk (Bukhari 5837). Ibn Majah 3414 adds that these are for the unbelievers in this world and for the believers in the Hereafter.
must_not: limiting it to women
notes: Applies as stated in the reports.

question: is gold jewellery allowed for men?
gold_answer: Abu Musa reported the Prophet said gold and silk are permitted for women of his community and forbidden for men (Nasai 5148). Ali's report shows the Prophet holding silk and gold and calling them forbidden for the males of the Ummah (Nasai 5144).
must_not: saying it is allowed for men
notes: Clear in these texts; extent for items like watches or fillings is not covered here.

question: What does the Quran tell women and men about covering and lowering the gaze?
gold_answer: Surah 24:30 tells believing men to lower their gaze and be modest. Surah 24:31 tells believing women likewise, to display of their adornment only what is apparent, to draw their veils over their bosoms, and lists whom they may reveal adornment to (husbands, fathers, sons, brothers and others named). Verse 24:60 relaxes outer clothing for elderly women past marriage, though refraining is better.
must_not: claiming the verse specifies a particular garment name
notes: Pickthall translation.

question: do women have to cover their face and hands in front of non-mahram men? i get different answers from different people
gold_answer: Texts used in the discussion: 24:31 allows only what is apparent of adornment to be shown and tells women to draw veils over their bosoms; 33:59 tells the Prophet's wives, daughters and believing women to draw their cloaks close when they go abroad. A report in Abu Dawud 4104 has the Prophet telling Asma that a woman who reaches puberty should not show her body except 'this and this', pointing to his face and hands, though Abu Dawud himself calls it mursal (a link missing). Scholars disagree on how to interpret 'what is apparent' and on that report's strength; the corpus does not settle it.
must_not: declaring one view as the only valid opinion
notes: Disputed. Abu Dawud flags the chain as mursal in the corpus text.

question: Is it haram for a woman to wear perfume when she goes outside?
gold_answer: Abu Musa al-Ash'ari reported that the Prophet said any woman who puts on perfume and passes by people so that they smell her fragrance is an adulteress (Nasai 5126; Tirmidhi 2786 has a parallel narration about passing a gathering).
must_not: saying women may never use perfume at home
notes: The hadith concerns going out to be smelled by men, not private use.

question: Can a woman travel alone for hajj or work without a mahram?
gold_answer: Abu Huraira reported that the Prophet said it is not lawful for a woman who believes in Allah and the Last Day to travel a day and night except with a mahram (Bukhari 1088; Muslim 3266 'a night's journey'). Reports vary in the period mentioned (one day/night or three days in Bukhari 1087). How modern travel fits this is something scholars address.
must_not: stating a single number of kilometers
notes: Narrations vary on the duration; the gold avoids picking one.

question: what did the prophet mean by saying the in-law (hamu) is death?
gold_answer: When the Prophet warned 'Beware of entering upon women', a man of the Ansar asked about al-hamu (the husband's in-laws such as his brother). The Prophet answered that the hamu is death (Bukhari 5232, Tirmidhi 1171).
must_not: permitting being alone with the brother in law
notes: Strong warning about seclusion; scholars explain the wording as warning of the risk.

question: Is music haram? someone showed me a hadith and someone else showed me the Eid hadith
gold_answer: One set of texts: Bukhari 5590 reports the Prophet saying some of his people would treat illegal sexual intercourse, silk, alcohol and musical instruments as lawful. Another: on Eid, Aisha had two girls singing and beating the duff; Abu Bakr rebuked them but the Prophet said to leave them, for every people has a festival (Nasai 1593; Ibn Majah 1898). Scholars differ on how to reconcile these and on which instruments and occasions are covered.
must_not: declaring a verdict as agreed by all
notes: Highly disputed topic; the corpus gives hadith evidence on both sides.

question: Does verse 31:6 about 'idle talk' prove music is haram?
gold_answer: Verse 31:6 (Pickthall) condemns the one who pays for mere pastime of discourse to mislead from Allah's way without knowledge and mock it, and promises a shameful doom. The text itself describes misleading from Allah's way and mockery; it does not name music, so applying it to music depends on interpretation and on other evidences, on which scholars differ.
must_not: claiming the verse mentions music by name
notes: Corpus has no tafsir; the answer sticks to the translation's wording.

question: are photos and pictures of living things haram in islam? and dolls?
gold_answer: Texts: Abu Talha reported the Prophet saying angels do not enter a house that has a dog or a picture (Bukhari 3322); Abu Juhaifa's report says the Prophet cursed the makers of pictures (Bukhari 5347); on the other side, Aisha played with dolls in the Prophet's presence (Bukhari 6130), whose editor note says such play was allowed for her as a young girl. Scholars differ over what these cover (statues, drawings, photographs); the corpus does not settle it.
must_not: saying all images are equally forbidden by consensus
notes: Disputed scope, the Bukhari 6130 note is a translator comment in the corpus.

question: Should a man grow his beard? what is the hadith
gold_answer: Ibn Umar reported the Prophet saying to trim the moustache closely and let the beard grow (Muslim 600), and Abu Huraira's report adds 'act against the fire-worshippers' (Muslim 603). Scholars discuss whether the command is obligatory or recommended.
must_not: saying shaving is mentioned as lawful in these reports
notes: Ruling strength is debated; gold gives the texts.

question: are tattoos haram?
gold_answer: Abdullah ibn Mas'ud reported that the Messenger of Allah cursed the woman who tattoos and the one who is tattooed (Nasai 3416), and another report adds 'for the purpose of beautification' (Nasai 5102).
must_not: saying tattoos are merely disliked
notes: Whether a medical tattoo or a permanent makeup differs is not in the texts.

question: Does saying 'you are divorced' three times in one sitting count as three talaqs or one?
gold_answer: Two lines of evidence appear. Muslim 3675 and Abu Dawud 2199 report Ibn Abbas saying three pronouncements together were treated as one in the time of the Prophet and Abu Bakr, until Umar made them operative because people did it a lot. The Quran (2:229-230) speaks of divorce 'twice' and then a third after which she is not lawful until she marries another husband. Scholars differ on whether Umar's ruling stands; consult a qualified scholar for your case.
must_mention: one in the time of the Prophet
must_not: picking one position as the only valid one
notes: Disputed. Strongly sensitive; legal effect also depends on local law.

question: my husband divorced me when i was on my period, is that allowed?
gold_answer: Ibn Umar divorced his wife during her period; Umar told the Prophet, who ordered him to take her back and divorce her when she was pure (not menstruating) or pregnant (Ibn Majah 2023, Bukhari 5258). So divorce during menses is contrary to the instructed way. Whether it counts as a divorce is discussed by scholars.
must_not: saying it is the recommended time
notes: Bukhari 5258 includes a question whether it counted; the answer in the text is ambiguous.

question: how long is the iddah for a divorced woman and for a widow?
gold_answer: Surah 2:228 says divorced women wait three monthly courses. Surah 2:234 says widows wait four months and ten days.
must_not: saying all women wait the same period
notes: Pregnant women are outside this answer; not asserted here.

question: can a wife get a divorce from her husband if she hates him? what is khul?
gold_answer: Thabit ibn Qais's wife told the Prophet she did not fault his character or religion but could not endure living with him; he asked 'Will you return his garden?', she agreed, and he ordered Thabit to divorce her (Bukhari 5275, 5274). Surah 2:229 allows the woman to ransom herself when both fear they cannot keep Allah's limits.
must_not: saying the woman has no way out
notes: Basis of khul.

question: Is a marriage valid without the wali? Hanafis and others differ, I'm confused.
gold_answer: Evidence for requiring the guardian: Aisha reported the Prophet saying a woman who marries without her guardian's arrangement has an invalid marriage, thrice (Ibn Majah 1879), and Abu Musa reported 'no marriage without a guardian' (Abu Dawud 2085). On the other side of the discussion, Ibn Abbas reported the Prophet saying a previously married woman has more right to decide about herself than her guardian, and a virgin is asked for permission (Nasai 3260). Scholars differ on how to combine these; the corpus does not say which school holds what.
must_not: attributing to a school without a source
notes: Disputed; the school names in the question are not backed by the corpus so the gold avoids them.

question: Does a woman have to agree to her marriage? Can parents force it?
gold_answer: Abu Huraira reported the Prophet said a previously married woman must not be married until her consent is sought, and a virgin not until her permission is sought; her permission can be her silence (Bukhari 6970, Nasai 3267).
must_not: saying parents may force a marriage
notes: Clear that consent is required.

question: What is the minimum mahr? Does it have to be money?
gold_answer: The Prophet told a man to marry even with an iron ring (Bukhari 5150), and in another account, when the man had nothing, he agreed to marry the woman to him with what he knew of the Quran (Bukhari 5132). Surah 4:4 says to give women their marriage portions as a free gift.
must_not: stating a fixed minimum amount
notes: Texts show a very modest mahr; no fixed amount asserted.

question: Sunni say mut'a marriage was banned, Shia say it's allowed. What do the hadith books say?
gold_answer: Sunni hadith collections in the corpus report that the Prophet forbade temporary marriage on the day of Khaibar (Ali, Muslim 5005) and that Sabra al-Juhani heard him say he had permitted it but Allah had now forbidden it until the Day of Resurrection (Muslim 3422). Other groups follow different reports and interpretations that are not in this corpus, so the corpus can only state what these hadith say.
must_not: claiming consensus of all sects
notes: Neutral: cites only the Muslim reports; Shia sources not in corpus.

question: What does Surah An-Nisa 4:3 say about having more than one wife?
gold_answer: Verse 4:3 says that if you fear you cannot deal fairly with orphans, marry women who seem good to you, two, three or four; but if you fear you cannot do justice, then only one (or captives). Verse 4:129 says you will not be able to deal equally between wives however much you wish, but do not turn altogether away from one.
must_not: saying there is no condition
notes: Pickthall translation; how scholars combine 4:3 and 4:129 is a further discussion.

question: explain verse 4:34 about men being in charge of women and the beating part. is it permission for domestic violence?
gold_answer: Verse 4:34 says men are in charge of women because Allah has favoured some over others and because men spend of their property; it describes good women as obedient, guarding in secret, and for those from whom one fears rebellion gives steps: admonish, banish to beds apart, and 'scourge' (as Pickthall renders it). 4:19 commands consorting with women in kindness, the Prophet said the best of you is best to his wife (Ibn Majah 1977), and he said that when one beats, he should avoid the face (Abu Dawud 4493, a general hadith on beating). Interpreters differ on the meaning and limits of this verse; refer to a scholar.
must_not: presenting the verse as a licence to harm
notes: Highly sensitive. Abu Dawud 4493 is a general hadith on beating, listed as acceptable.

question: Why does the Quran say two women witnesses in 2:282?
gold_answer: Verse 2:282 concerns contracting a debt for a fixed term: record it in writing and call to witness two men from among you, and if two men are not available then a man and two women from those you approve as witnesses. The part of the verse the translation cites gives the reason as one of them erring and the other reminding. The verse speaks of debts; extending it to every case is a scholarly question.
must_not: saying a woman's testimony is always half
notes: Pickthall translation; clause on two women and the reason (one erring, the other reminding) is in the verse text.

question: do sons get double what daughters get in inheritance? why
gold_answer: Surah 4:11 says to the male the equivalent of the portion of two females, and for daughters only: two-thirds if more than two, half if one; each parent gets a sixth if there is a son. Ibn Abbas in Bukhari 4578 explained that before Islam children took everything and parents only through a will, and Allah decreed the son's share twice the daughter's.
must_not: claiming equal shares for sons and daughters
notes: Quranic rule; wisdom for it is not given in these passages.

question: If someone dies with no children and has a sister, what does she inherit?
gold_answer: Surah 4:176 says that if a man dies childless and has a sister, hers is half the heritage; two sisters get two-thirds; and brothers and sisters together, the male gets the equivalent of two females. The Prophet also said to give the fixed shares to those entitled and the remainder to the nearest male heir (Muslim 4143).
must_not: claiming a sister gets everything
notes: Complex inheritance cases need a mufti.

question: can i leave my whole wealth to charity in my will?
gold_answer: Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, who had only a daughter as heir, asked about giving two-thirds, then half, and was told no; for one third, the Prophet said one third is a lot, and leaving heirs rich is better than leaving them poor and begging (Ibn Majah 2708). Surah 4:11 also frames inheritance after any bequest or debt.
must_not: saying any amount can be willed
notes: Gold avoids saying whether one third is the legal cap beyond what the hadith shows.

question: can a muslim inherit from his non muslim father?
gold_answer: Usama ibn Zaid reported the Prophet saying a Muslim does not inherit from a non-Muslim and a non-Muslim does not inherit from a Muslim (Muslim 4140, Tirmidhi 2107).
must_not: saying it is allowed
notes: Some scholars discuss exceptions; the gold gives the hadith text only.

question: What is the ruling on someone who leaves Islam? Is it death or not?
gold_answer: Texts: Ibn Abbas reported the Prophet said 'Whoever changes his religion, kill him' (Nasai 4059). Ibn Mas'ud's hadith says a Muslim's blood is not lawful except in three cases, including the one who leaves the religion and the community (Bukhari 6878). Others point to 2:256, 'There is no compulsion in religion'. Scholars differ on how to read these, including on the circumstances and procedures; seek a scholar.
must_not: claiming a single uncontested position
notes: Disputed and sensitive; Bukhari 6878 text continues 'the one who reverts from Islam and leaves the community'.

question: Does the Quran allow forcing people to become Muslim?
gold_answer: Surah 2:256 says there is no compulsion in religion; right direction is distinct from error. Surah 109:6 says 'Unto you your religion, and unto me my religion.'
must_not: saying conversion by force is commanded
notes: Context for other verses on fighting is a separate question.

question: is it permitted to kill a non-muslim who lives in a muslim country under a treaty?
gold_answer: No. The Prophet said whoever kills a mu'ahid (one with a covenant) has violated Allah's and His Messenger's covenant and will not smell the fragrance of Paradise (Tirmidhi 1403; Bukhari 6914).
must_not: permitting harm to protected non-Muslims
notes: Clear and strong.

question: in war, can civilians like women and kids be targeted?
gold_answer: A woman was found killed in one of the Prophet's battles, and the Prophet forbade the killing of women and children (Bukhari 3014, Muslim 4548).
must_not: allowing targeting of civilians
notes: Extending the rule to all civilians is a scholarly step; gold limits to women and children.

question: what does surah 9:5 'slay the idolaters' really mean? isn't it about killing all non-muslims?
gold_answer: Verse 9:5 commands slaying idolaters after the sacred months passed, unless they repent, establish prayer and pay the poor-due. Other verses limit it: 2:190 says fight those who fight you but begin not hostilities, 'Allah loveth not aggressors', and 8:61 says if they incline to peace, incline to it. Interpreters discuss the context of this verse (idolaters who broke treaties) and its relation to the others; the corpus has no tafsir text to settle it.
must_not: claiming the verse commands killing all non-Muslims
notes: Sensitive; the gold avoids asserting context outside the corpus.

question: does the quran say to be kind to non-muslims?
gold_answer: Verse 60:8 says Allah does not forbid you to show kindness and deal justly with those who did not fight you over religion or drive you out of your homes; Allah loves the just. Verse 60:9 forbids friendship only with those who fought you over religion and drove you out.
must_not: saying the Quran forbids dealing with all non-Muslims
notes: Pickthall translation.

question: What does Surah Al-Ma'idah 5:32 say about killing one person?
gold_answer: Verse 5:32 says that for that cause it was decreed for the Children of Israel that whoever kills a human being other than for manslaughter or corruption in the earth, it is as if he killed all mankind, and whoever saves one life, as if he saved all mankind.
must_mention: as if he had killed all mankind
must_not: restricting it to Muslims
notes: Also relevant to discussions about jihad; verse addressed to Children of Israel.

question: What does verse 9:29 say and who is it about? People quote it a lot.
gold_answer: Verse 9:29 says to fight those who were given the Scripture who do not believe in Allah nor the Last Day, do not forbid what Allah and His Messenger forbade, and do not follow the Religion of Truth, until they pay the tribute readily, being brought low. Its historical context and application are discussed by interpreters and legal scholars; the corpus gives the verse but no tafsir, so conditions beyond the text are not asserted.
must_not: saying it commands fighting every Christian or Jew in every era
notes: Sensitive; gold deliberately limited to the text.

question: Did the Prophet show respect to non-Muslim funerals?
gold_answer: Jabir reported that a funeral passed and the Prophet stood up; when told it was a Jew's, he said 'Whenever you see a funeral procession, you should stand up' (Bukhari 1311). Nasai 1928 reports the Prophet and Companions standing for a Jew's funeral.
notes: Whether standing is still required is a different question.

question: Can a Muslim man marry a Christian or Jewish woman? what about an idolater?
gold_answer: Verse 5:5 makes lawful the virtuous women of those who received the Scripture, when given their marriage portions. Verse 2:221 forbids marrying idolatresses until they believe and giving Muslim women to idolaters. Scholars differ on details such as present-day applicability.
must_not: permitting marriage to idolatresses
notes: Pickthall translation; marriage of Muslim women to People of the Book is not covered by 5:5 text.

question: what if my parents tell me to do something against Islam? do i still obey them
gold_answer: Verses 31:15 and 29:8 say that if parents strive to make you join with Allah what you have no knowledge of, do not obey them, yet consort with them kindly in the world.
must_not: cutting off parents completely
notes: Both obedience limits and kindness remain.

question: Why is the mother mentioned three times in the hadith about who deserves best treatment?
gold_answer: A man asked who was most entitled to his best companionship; the Prophet said 'your mother' three times and only the fourth time 'your father' (Bukhari 5971). In Nasai 3104 he told a man wanting to go to jihad to stay with his mother, as Paradise is beneath her feet.
must_not: saying the father is ahead of the mother
notes: Hadith content only; the 'beneath her feet' phrase is in Nasai 3104 narrator wording.

question: What does the Quran say about treating old parents?
gold_answer: Verse 17:23 says Allah decreed worship of none but Him and kindness to parents; if one or both reach old age, do not say 'Fie' to them nor repulse them, but speak a gracious word. Verse 17:24 adds lowering the wing of submission through mercy and praying 'My Lord, have mercy on them both as they cared for me when I was little'.

question: I swore an oath and broke it. what's the kaffara?
gold_answer: Verse 5:89 says the expiation is feeding ten needy people with the average of what you feed your own family, or clothing them, or freeing a slave. Bukhari 6621 reports Abu Bakr saying that if he swears and finds something better, he does the better and makes expiation.
must_not: saying no expiation is due
notes: The fasting alternative at the end of 5:89 is outside the snippet read; not asserted.

question: can i swear by my father or by the kaaba?
gold_answer: Ibn Umar heard a man say 'No, by the Ka'bah' and said nothing is sworn by other than Allah, because the Prophet said whoever swears by other than Allah has committed disbelief or shirk (Tirmidhi 1535). Thabit ibn Ad-Dahhak reported that swearing by a religion other than Islam falsely makes one as he says (Bukhari 6652).
must_not: calling it permissible
notes: Scholars discuss the nature (minor shirk). Not asserted beyond the wording.

question: do accidental oaths count? like saying 'by Allah' without meaning
gold_answer: Verse 2:225 says Allah will not take you to task for what is unintentional in your oaths, but for what your hearts have garnered. Verse 2:224 says not to make Allah by your oaths a hindrance to righteousness and making peace.

question: Is magic (sihr) real in Islam? does the Quran say anything about it?
gold_answer: Verse 2:102 says devils taught mankind magic and what was revealed to the two angels Harut and Marut in Babel. Nasai 4079 reports the Prophet saying whoever ties a knot and blows on it has practised magic, and whoever practises magic has committed shirk. Bukhari 3268 reports that the Prophet himself was bewitched by Labid, so that he fancied doing something he had not done.
must_not: permitting magic for healing
notes: Sensitive; Bukhari 3268 account is of the Prophet being affected, not of him being corrupted.

question: Is going to a fortune teller or horoscope reader a sin?
gold_answer: Safiyya reported from some of the wives that the Prophet said whoever visits a diviner ('arraf) and asks him about anything, his prayers will not be accepted for forty nights (Muslim 5821). Abu Mas'ud reported the Prophet forbade the payment made to a fortune-teller (Tirmidhi 1133).
must_not: saying it is harmless
notes: The hadith text itself.

question: what are jinn made of according to Quran and hadith
gold_answer: The Quran says the jinn were created from smokeless fire (55:15). Aisha reported the Prophet said angels were created from light, jinn from a spark of fire, and Adam from what was described to you (clay) (Muslim 7495).
must_not: saying jinn are made of clay

question: Will the Prophet intercede for people on the Day of Judgement? Isn't intercession shirk?
gold_answer: Verse 20:109 says on that day no intercession avails except that of him whom the Beneficent has given leave and whose word He accepts; 2:255 asks 'Who is he that intercedes with Him save by His leave?'. The Prophet said the luckiest to gain his intercession will be the one who said sincerely 'None has the right to be worshipped but Allah' (Bukhari 99), and that his intercession is for those of his people who committed major sins (Abu Dawud 4739).
must_not: saying intercession is independent of Allah's leave
notes: Intercession is conditioned on Allah's leave.

question: Is asking righteous dead people or saints to intercede for you shirk? Some say yes, some say no.
gold_answer: Verse 10:18 criticises those who worship beside Allah what neither harms nor benefits them, saying 'These are our intercessors with Allah', and 39:3 describes those who take protecting friends besides Allah, saying they only worship them to bring them nearer to Allah, and says Allah does not guide a liar and ingrate. 2:255 says no one intercedes with Him except by His leave. Scholars differ on whether and how particular practices of seeking intercession fall under these verses; the corpus does not settle those cases.
must_not: declaring all Muslims who disagree disbelievers
notes: Disputed application. Gold avoids takfir.

question: What does 'every innovation is misguidance' mean? Is any new thing bid'ah?
gold_answer: Aisha reported the Prophet said whoever innovates something in this matter that is not part of it will have it rejected (Ibn Majah 14, Bukhari 2697). Ibn Majah 203 reports he said whoever introduces a good practice that is followed receives its reward and the reward of those who follow it, and whoever introduces a bad one bears its sin. Scholars differ on how these texts apply to new practices, notably whether any innovations are 'good'.
must_not: saying all novelties are the same by consensus
notes: Disputed concept; both texts are quoted.

question: If Allah is not like anything, how do we understand verses about Allah's attributes? (42:11, 3:7)
gold_answer: Verse 42:11 says 'Naught is as His likeness; and He is the Hearer, the Seer.' Verse 3:7 says some verses are clear and others allegorical, that those with doubt in their hearts pursue the allegorical seeking dissension, and that the people of sound instruction say 'We believe therein; the whole is from our Lord'. Scholars differ on how to read the allegorical verses on attributes; the corpus does not state the schools' positions.
must_not: reducing the matter to a single school's view
notes: The translation's reading of 3:7 (None knoweth its explanation save Allah) is used as stated.

question: Does verse 3:85 mean only Muslims enter Paradise? And what about 2:62?
gold_answer: Verse 3:85 says whoever seeks a religion other than the Surrender (Islam) will not have it accepted from him and will be a loser. Verse 2:62 says those who believe, and the Jews, Christians and Sabaeans, whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day and does right, their reward is with their Lord. Interpreters differ on how these combine, including whether 2:62 refers to a time before the Prophet; the corpus has no tafsir so no resolution is asserted.
must_mention: believes in Allah and the Last Day
must_not: picking one view as certain
notes: Highly sensitive.

question: What did the Prophet say at Ghadir Khumm about Ali, and why do Sunnis and Shia read it differently?
gold_answer: Tirmidhi 3713 reports the Prophet said 'For whomever I am his mawla, Ali is his mawla.' The word mawla has more than one usage in the hadith collections (for example Tirmidhi 3940 uses it of the tribes and says Allah and His Messenger are their mawla). The disagreement is about what 'mawla' means here; the corpus gives the text but not the schools' interpretations.
must_not: claiming the Prophet explicitly named a successor in these wordings
notes: Neutral. Don't state either side as settled.

question: What is the hadith of the two weighty things and who are the Ahl al-Bayt in it?
gold_answer: Zayd ibn Arqam reported in Muslim 6225 that at Khumm the Prophet said he was leaving two weighty things: the Book of Allah and the members of his household, and he reminded them of their duties to his family. Asked who they are, Zayd said his wives are of his family but here it means those for whom accepting zakat is forbidden: the families of Ali, Aqil, Ja'far and Abbas.
must_mention: those for whom zakat is forbidden
must_not: limiting the household to the wives only
notes: Wording is from this Muslim narration; other narrations differ and are not in the corpus.

question: Sunnis and Shia both quote 'Ali is to me as Harun was to Musa'. What does the text say?
gold_answer: Sa'd reported the Prophet said to Ali, 'Aren't you satisfied with being unto me what Aaron was unto Moses?' (Muslim 6221, Bukhari 3706). Readers differ on its significance; the corpus has the text only.
must_not: adding a clause 'except there is no prophet after me' as a certain part of these narrations
notes: Wording in these narrations is short; other narrations add context not in these passages.

question: Is it okay to insult the Companions of the Prophet?
gold_answer: Ibn Umar reported the Prophet said, 'If you see those who abuse my Companions, then say: May Allah's curse be upon the worst of you' (Tirmidhi 3866). The ruling on particular cases is for scholars, and Muslim groups differ in how they view individual Companions.
must_not: claiming all groups agree on how to judge each Companion
notes: Only one hadith is quoted; this narration's grading is not asserted here.

question: Is backbiting only about telling lies?
gold_answer: No. The Prophet defined backbiting as mentioning your brother with what he dislikes; asked if it counts when what is said is true, he said that if it is true you have backbitten him and if untrue you have slandered him (Muslim 6593, Tirmidhi 1934). Verse 49:12 says not to backbite one another, likening it to eating the flesh of your dead brother.
must_mention: mentioning your brother with what he dislikes
must_not: saying only false statements are backbiting
notes: Hadith text read in corpus; Tirmidhi 1934 parallel is not in sources.

question: how to control anger according to hadith
gold_answer: The Prophet said the strong person is not the one who wrestles well, but the one who controls himself in a fit of rage (Muslim 6643, Bukhari 6114).

question: What is the definition of a Muslim in the hadith about the tongue and hand?
gold_answer: A Muslim is the one from whose tongue and hand Muslims are safe (Muslim 162, Tirmidhi 2627).

question: Is committing suicide a sin? what happens to a person who does that?
gold_answer: The Prophet warned that whoever commits suicide by a method will keep punishing himself by that method in Hell (Bukhari 1365, Bukhari 6652). These reports do not decide any specific person's fate, which belongs to Allah; anyone struggling should seek help from people they trust and professionals.
must_not: declaring any specific person damned
notes: Sensitive: emphasise seeking help and avoid declaring individuals' fate.

question: does the quran allow not fasting if you're old or ill?
gold_answer: Verse 2:184 says the sick or the traveller fast the same number of other days, and for those who can afford it there is a ransom: the feeding of a man in need. Muslim 2686 reports that before the verse making the fast of Ramadan obligatory was revealed, people could break and feed a needy person as expiation.
must_not: saying the elderly are never allowed to skip
notes: Application to the elderly is a ruling; gold limited to the verse.

question: what time should i stop eating suhoor? and is suhoor needed?
gold_answer: Verse 2:187 says to eat and drink until the white thread becomes distinct from the black thread of dawn, then fast until nightfall. Amr ibn al-As reported the Prophet saying the difference between our fasting and that of the People of the Book is eating shortly before dawn (Muslim 2550).
must_not: saying eating after dawn is allowed
notes: Exact times by calendar are not in the texts.

question: when to break the fast, as soon as maghrib adhan?
gold_answer: Umar reported that when night falls from the east, day vanishes from the west and the sun sets, the fasting person should break the fast (Bukhari 1954). Abu Huraira reported the Prophet saying people stay in good as long as they hasten to break the fast (Ibn Majah 1698).
must_not: saying delay is better
notes: Clear.

question: Is donkey meat halal? I read that the Prophet banned it at Khaibar, but I also read Ibn Abbas didn't think so.
gold_answer: Ali reported the Prophet forbade the flesh of domestic asses on the Day of Khaibar (Muslim 5005). Bukhari 5529 reports that Ibn Abbas would not give a final verdict that it was forbidden and recited 6:145, 'I find not in that which has been inspired to me anything forbidden to be eaten unless it be carrion, blood, swine flesh...'. The latter cites the Quran's list; others rely on the Prophet's ban. Scholars differ in weighing them.
must_not: denying the hadith exists
notes: Muslim 5005 is also cited in the mut'a item; check the limit of two uses.

question: What does the hadith say about neighbours?
gold_answer: The Prophet said that Jibril kept advising him about the neighbour until he thought the neighbour would be made an heir (Ibn Majah 3673, 3674). Abdullah ibn Amr told his family to give a gift of a slaughtered sheep to his Jewish neighbour on this basis (Abu Dawud 5152).

question: Is it true the Prophet was affected by sihr? isn't that against his being protected?
gold_answer: Aisha reported that magic was worked on the Prophet so that he fancied doing a thing he had not done (Bukhari 3175, 6063). In Bukhari 6063 two men in his dream name the man behind it (Lubaid), the materials (a comb with hair and date-palm pollen) and the well of Dharwan. Interpreters discuss the extent of its effect; the reports describe him imagining he had done things he had not, and that he was cured.
must_not: saying it affected his delivery of revelation
notes: Sensitive. Bukhari 3268 is a further narration.

question: what can be given for zakat al fitr and how much
gold_answer: Ibn Umar reported the Messenger of Allah prescribed Zakat-ul-Fitr as one sa' of dates or one sa' of barley on every slave or free person, young or old (Muslim 2279). Abu Sa'id al-Khudri said they used to give one sa' of food, barley, dates, cottage cheese or raisins (Bukhari 1506).
must_not: claiming it is only for adults
notes: Converting a sa' to modern weights is not in the texts.

question: do i have to make wudu again after eating camel meat?
gold_answer: Reports from Bara' and Abdullah ibn Amr say the Prophet commanded ablution after eating camel meat and not after eating mutton (Ibn Majah 497; Abu Dawud 184). Scholars discuss whether this means full ablution and whether it still applies; the texts are as quoted.
must_not: saying ablution is needed after all meats
notes: Hadith-only answer; do not assert school positions.

question: can muslims keep dogs as pets
gold_answer: Abu Huraira reported the Prophet said that whoever keeps a dog has a qirat of his reward deducted each day, unless it is for guarding crops or livestock (Bukhari 2322); Nasai 4291 lists herding, hunting and farming as exceptions.
must_not: saying pet dogs are rewarded
notes: Hadith text only; scholars discuss other uses (guarding homes, etc.).

question: Is it okay to build a mosque over a saint's grave? I see it in many countries
gold_answer: Abu Huraira reported the Prophet said 'May Allah's curse be on the Jews, for they built places of worship at the graves of their Prophets' (Bukhari 437); Muslim 1186 adds the Christians. How this applies to particular shrines is discussed by scholars, and the corpus does not settle the particular cases.
must_not: declaring all visitors of graves disbelievers
notes: Sensitive; gold sticks to the text.
